objective: Turn the controlled BMS state and transition CSV baseline into an executable fail-closed validator and deterministic engineering report without claiming physical battery safety evidence.
decision_supported: Can CI reject missing, duplicated, reordered, or illegal BMS protection paths while preserving DESIGN_BASELINE_ONLY and NOT_EXECUTED release truth?
acceptance: The parser rejects duplicate state names and duplicate source-state/event keys, and accepts only the declared CSV headers and fields.
Every source and target is a known state; contactor actions, latch values, reset authorities, and guards are controlled and non-empty.
Every state has an explicit fault/default behavior and the complete controlled state policy is checked.
The legal transition graph is complete and deterministic; deleting any required safety transition or adding an illegal edge fails validation.
FAULT_LATCHED can recover only through an explicit guarded local_reset to SELF_TEST; automatic recovery and unsafe RUN entry are rejected.
The generated report includes a deterministic transition-table SHA-256 and preserves DESIGN_BASELINE_ONLY, NOT_EXECUTED, release_ready=false, and physical_results=NOT_EXECUTED.
The existing operations-readiness validator consumes the strict BMS report while retaining the broader EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED status.
No firmware, robot-control, MCU protocol, public interface, supplier, certification, or physical HIL claim is added.
evidence: Generated BMS report with structural checks, stable state/transition hashes, and explicit release blockers.
Focused hardware tests covering malformed tables, illegal edges, deleted transitions, fault-latch recovery, deterministic ordering, and status truthfulness.
Operations-readiness, full test, contract, scenario, context, and whitespace-check output.
stop_conditions: A firmware, MCU, robot-control, public interface, or safety-authority behavior change is required.
Supplier thresholds, pack identity, certification, or physical HIL evidence would need to be invented.
The controlled CSV baseline itself needs semantic changes rather than executable validation.
A generated result would promote NOT_EXECUTED or DESIGN_BASELINE_ONLY to a physical or production PASS.
Task Packet validation reports a changed path outside allowed_paths.
risks_and_fallbacks: The validator intentionally encodes the current reviewed baseline; any future transition change requires an explicit owner-reviewed update to the validator and its mutation tests.
A structural pass proves table integrity only. Electrical/Safety Owner approval, supplier data, calibrated measurements, and physical fault injection remain release gates.
If privileged hardware evidence is unavailable, retain NOT_EXECUTED and ship only the repository-side report.
